takeaway: Thoracic duct: starts from the cisterna chyli at T12, rises between aorta and azygos, turns left at T5 behind the oesophagus, ends at the left internal jugular-subclavian confluence.

lines.text: Which statement about the thoracic duct is correct?
It begins at the end of the cisterna chyli, at T12, not T10.
lines.say: (clears throat) It begins at the end of the cisterna chyli, at T twelve, not T ten.

lines.text: It passes up between the aorta and the azygos vein, not the vena cava.
At T5 it turns to the left, passing behind the oesophagus.
lines.say: At T five it turns to the left, passing behind the oesophagus.

lines.text: It arches over the left pleura to join the left internal jugular and subclavian veins.
So the answer: in adults it carries up to 4 L of lymph a day.
lines.say: So the answer: in adults it carries up to four litres of lymph a day.

lines.text: The right lymphatic duct drains only the right upper body, not the lower limb.
